name: Áine Kennedy

education.notes: Studied entrepreneurship at Maynooth alongside running retail beauty jobs.

keyDecisions: Started working in beauty retail at 16 (Boots) and stacked Benefit Cosmetics + Tanorganic — eight years of front-line consumer-beauty reps before founding.
Studied entrepreneurship at Maynooth in parallel — academic credentials layered onto operating reps, not the other way round.
lessons: Front-line retail reps in your eventual category are the cheapest possible customer-research — you know what customers actually buy because you sold to them in person.
Beauty is one of few categories where you can be a credible founder with sales-floor experience instead of a CV.
Stacking real jobs across multiple beauty brands (Boots, Benefit, Tanorganic) compounds pattern-recognition cheaply in your late teens.
careerSteps.notes: Per Goss / Irish Times / Beauty Independent coverage.

keyDecisions: Started making TikTok videos with her grandad during Covid — accidentally built a consumer-brand-ready distribution channel before having a product.
lessons: Personal audience built during downtime (Covid) is the cheapest pre-product distribution asset a consumer founder can have.
Family creative collaborations (grandad on camera) are credible and durable — they don't churn like influencer arrangements.

keyDecisions: Invested her $12k house deposit to launch The Smooth Company from her attic in 2022 — explicit bet of personal capital instead of raising.
Stayed bootstrapped — profitable from the start, reinvesting profits rather than chasing dilutive capital.
Targeted the slick-back / hair-taming niche on TikTok before going global — used existing audience as launch lever.
Expanded into 92 countries via retailer relationships (Brown Thomas, De Bijenkorf, H&M) rather than relying purely on DTC ads.
lessons: Bootstrapped + profitable + viral-distribution is a complete consumer-brand playbook — does not require VC.
Multi-channel retail (DTC + premium department stores + H&M-tier) gives revenue stability and credibility that DTC-only brands lack.
Tripling revenue year-over-year while staying profitable is the operating signal that makes investors come to you, not the other way round.
Self-funded with a $12k house deposit is a viable founding capital base — capital efficiency is the moat, not the deck.
careerSteps.notes: Founded 2022. Products sold in 92 countries; stocked by Brown Thomas, De Bijenkorf, H&M and others. Revenue tripled 2023→2024 per Irish Times. EY Emerging Entrepreneur of the Year (Nov 2025); Future Leader at Irish Times Business Awards. Forbes 30 Under 30 Europe 2026.

outcomes.currentStatus: Founder & CEO of The Smooth Company (Dublin). Bootstrapped DTC haircare brand sold in 92 countries; tripled revenue 2023→2024; profitable from start. EY Emerging Entrepreneur 2025.

lessons.lesson: Bootstrapped + profitable + 92-country retail distribution is a complete consumer-brand playbook with no VC required.
Eight years of front-line beauty retail (Boots, Benefit, Tanorganic) starting at 16 is the cheapest customer-research possible — beauty-floor reps beat any MBA.
Personal TikTok audience built during Covid (with grandad on camera) became the pre-product distribution asset that launched the brand.
A $12k house deposit can be a viable founding capital base — capital efficiency is the moat, not the deck.
